skill.name: ai-podcast-creation
skill.description: Create AI podcast episodes with text-to-speech voices, generated music, and audio merging through inference.sh workflows.
skill.summary: Build narrated, multi-voice, and music-backed podcast audio with inference.sh tools.
skill.author: inference-sh

security_audit.summary: Most static external command detections are Markdown backticks or code fences, so they are false positives. The installer command on line 21 is confirmed as critical because it pipes a remote script directly into sh, and the related installer URL is also security relevant. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed file.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to sh.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell installation with a signed package, checksum verification, or a documented manual install step that requires user review.

remediation.issue: Documented commands exceed the declared allowed-tools boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Keep executable examples within Bash(infsh *) or clearly mark curl and npx steps as manual setup outside automated skill execution.

remediation.issue: Document-to-podcast examples send user content to hosted model services.
remediation.suggestion: Add a privacy note telling users to remove confidential data before submitting documents or scripts to external services.

content.value_statement: Producing polished spoken audio can require scripting, voice generation, music, and editing tools. This skill organizes inference.sh workflows for narration, dialogue, music, and episode assembly.
actual_capabilities: Creates single-voice narration using Kokoro text-to-speech examples.
Builds multi-voice podcast conversations from separate host and guest segments.
Generates intro, outro, background music, and transition sounds through AI music examples.
Merges audio clips with crossfades and optional background audio using media-merger.
Includes script prompts for Claude-powered podcast dialogue and document discussions.
Provides reusable structures for interviews, solo episodes, and news roundups.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI, account access, and network connectivity.
Generated audio quality depends on the selected hosted model and input script quality.
Examples use external services, so confidential documents need separate privacy review.
The skill gives workflow guidance and does not replace detailed audio post-production software.

use_cases.title: Launch a Short Podcast Segment
use_cases.description: Turn a prepared script into a narrated audio segment with a chosen voice.

use_cases.title: Convert Research Into Discussion Audio
use_cases.description: Transform document notes into a two-host discussion for review or sharing.

use_cases.title: Prototype Branded Audio Updates
use_cases.description: Combine narration, intro music, outro music, and transitions for internal audio newsletters.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner Narration
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a simple spoken segment from a short script.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a one-minute narrated podcast segment from this script. Choose a clear voice, keep pacing natural, and return the generation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Two-Host Dialogue
prompt_templates.scenario: Make a topic feel conversational with two voices.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write and produce a two-host podcast dialogue about this topic. Separate host lines clearly and assign distinct voices.

prompt_templates.title: Music-Backed Episode Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Add intro music, background audio, and transitions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a five-minute podcast episode with intro music, narration, transition sounds, and outro music. Include the audio generation sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Document-to-Podcast Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert source material into a polished discussion format.
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize this document as a two-person podcast discussion. Create speaker turns, choose voices, add music cues, and define merge steps.

output_examples.input: A 90-second script about product roadmap highlights.
output_examples.output: A narrated episode plan with voice selection, generated audio segment, intro music, outro music, and merge instructions.

output_examples.input: A research brief that needs an accessible audio summary.
output_examples.output: A two-host dialogue outline, separate voice assignments, generated host segments, and a final merged discussion sequence.

output_examples.input: A weekly news roundup with three headlines.
output_examples.output: A structured roundup format with story sections, transition audio, natural pacing guidance, and final assembly steps.

best_practices: Review scripts before audio generation to remove errors, sensitive information, and awkward phrasing.
Use distinct voices for different speakers and keep speaker changes clearly labeled.
Keep background music quiet so speech remains understandable across listening devices.
anti_patterns: Do not send private documents to external models without an approved data handling process.
Do not combine many long segments before checking audio quality and pacing.
Do not use installation commands from the skill without verifying the source and integrity.

faq.question: Does this skill create a full podcast episode?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes workflows for scripts, voice generation, music, and audio merging.

faq.question: Which tools does it rely on?
faq.answer: It uses inference.sh apps for text-to-speech, AI music, media merging, and script generation.

faq.question: Can it create multi-voice conversations?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to generate separate host and guest segments, then merge them.

faq.question: Can I use my own documents?
faq.answer: Yes, but review privacy requirements before sending document content to external services.

faq.question: Does it edit audio locally?
faq.answer: No. It gives hosted inference.sh workflows and media-merger examples rather than local editing features.

faq.question: Is the installer command safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: No. The audit flags the remote installer pipeline as a critical command execution risk.
